## Mole-fraction state and its mixture totals (`ThermoX`) {#sec-ch03-thermo-x}

### Summary

Column models, adiabat construction and most offline analysis describe a parcel by temperature, pressure and mole
fractions, $(T, p, x)$. `ThermoX` works on that state. It converts mole fractions to concentrations and mass
fractions, computes density, heat capacity at constant pressure, enthalpy and entropy per unit volume, and inverts
the entropy for temperature at fixed pressure. Its `forward` method, the saturation adjustment at fixed temperature
and pressure, is the subject of @sec-ch04.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Conversions of the $(T, p, x)$ state; the mixture totals @eq-ch03-thermo-x-totals.

**Data.** $T$ [K], $p$ [Pa], $x_n$ [-] for all species; concentrations $c_n$ [mol m$^{-3}$].

**Placement.** Used by adiabat construction (@sec-ch03-adiabat) and by callers working in $(T, p, x)$.

**Activation.** API: `ThermoX(options)`, then `compute("<from>-><to>", [...])`.

**Guarantee / limits.** Exact except `TPX->V` with $z_n \ne 1$ and `PXS->T`, iterations to `ftol`.

**Evidence.** See the Tests layer.
:::

Local symbols: $C_p$, heat capacity at constant pressure per unit volume [J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$]; $H$, enthalpy per
unit volume [J m$^{-3}$]; $S$, entropy per unit volume [J m$^{-3}$ K$^{-1}$]. $\rho$, $\mu_n$ and $y_n$ are those
of @sec-ch03-thermo-y; $c_n$, $x_n$ and $N_{\mathrm g}$ those of @sec-ch03-eos.

The `compute` keys are named by inputs and output: `V` is the vector of concentrations $c_n$ here (not partial
densities as in `ThermoY`), `D` the density, `X` the mole fractions, `Y` the mass fractions.

### Derivation

**Mass fractions and density.** From $\rho_n = \mu_n c_n = \mu_n x_n c$,

$$
\begin{aligned}
y_n &= \frac{x_n \mu_n}{\sum_k x_k \mu_k}, \quad n \ge 1, \\
\rho &= \sum_n c_n \mu_n .
\end{aligned}
$$

`X->Y` computes the first line in `_xfrac_to_yfrac`; `V->D` the second in `_conc_to_dens`. Concentrations come
from @eq-ch03-eos-conc (`TPX->V`).

**Mixture totals.** As in @sec-ch03-thermo-y, each total is a concentration-weighted sum:

$$
\begin{aligned}
C_p &= \sum_n c_n c_{p,n}(T), \\
H &= \sum_n c_n h_n(T), \\
S &= \sum_n c_n s_n(T, p) .
\end{aligned}
$$ {#eq-ch03-thermo-x-totals}

The lines are computed in `_cp_vol` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoXImpl::_cp_vol >}}), `_enthalpy_vol`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoXImpl::_enthalpy_vol >}}) and `_entropy_vol`
({{< code src/thermo/thermo.hpp ThermoXImpl::_entropy_vol >}}). `THS->G` returns the Gibbs energy $H - T S$.

**Temperature from entropy at fixed pressure.** At fixed $p$ and fixed composition,
$\partial S / \partial T = C_p / T$. A Newton step on $S(T) = S_{\mathrm{given}}$ is therefore

$$
T \leftarrow T \left(1 + \frac{S_{\mathrm{given}} - S(T)}{C_p(T)}\right) ,
$$ {#eq-ch03-thermo-x-entropy-newton}

computed in `_entropy_to_temp` ({{< code src/thermo/thermo_x.cpp ThermoXImpl::_entropy_to_temp >}}). After each
step the code calls `forward`, the saturation adjustment at the new $(T, p)$, which changes the composition in place.
The slope $C_p$ is the frozen one of @eq-ch03-thermo-x-totals: it omits the latent heat of the condensation that
`forward` adds or removes, so in a saturated parcel the step is not the exact Newton step of the equilibrated
$S(T)$ (the effective heat capacity of @sec-ch03-adiabat is that slope).

### Numerical method

Every conversion is pointwise. `PXS->T` starts from $T = T_\star$ (`Tref`) in every cell and iterates
@eq-ch03-thermo-x-entropy-newton until $\max \lvert 1 - T_{\mathrm{old}}/T_{\mathrm{new}} \rvert$ is below `ftol` or `max_iter`
iterations are spent. Each iteration converts $x$ to $c$, evaluates $C_p$ and $S$, and runs one saturation
adjustment. `TPX->V` iterates only when a compressibility function is set (@sec-ch03-eos).

Tensor layout: mole fractions and concentrations are `(..., 1 + ny)` with the species last; mass fractions are
`(ny, ...)`, as in `ThermoY`.

The `ThermoX` figure is not provided: the figure module is not written yet.

: Code map of `ThermoX`. {#tbl-ch03-thermo-x-code}

Setup checks and warnings a user can hit: `X->Y` refuses an input whose species count is not the module's; an
unknown key is refused; `PXS->T` and `TPX->V` warn when `max_iter` is reached. On that warning both also write
their inputs to a file `thermo_x_entropy_to_temp_<time>.pt` or `thermo_x_xfrac_to_conc_<time>.pt` in the working
directory (verified by reading `_entropy_to_temp` and `_xfrac_to_conc` at the pin). `PXS->T` overwrites the mole
fractions it is given with the equilibrated ones.

| test (ctest name) | what it asserts | tolerance | where the tolerance comes from |
|---|---|---|---|
| `test_thermo.release` (`DeviceTest.thermo_x`) | `TPV->S` then `PXS->T` returns $T$ | $10^{-4}$ rel. and abs. | not yet derived |
| `test_thermo.release` (`DeviceTest.thermo_x`) | `V->D` equals concentration times molar mass, summed | $10^{-4}$ rel. and abs. | not yet derived |
| `test_thermo.release` (`DeviceTest.thermo_xy`) | `X->Y` then `Y->X` returns $x$ | $10^{-4}$ rel. and abs. | not yet derived |

: Tests of `ThermoX`. {#tbl-ch03-thermo-x-tests}

The tolerances are read from `tests/test_thermo.cpp` at the pin; their reason is missing evidence. The cases run on
CPU in float32 and float64 and on CUDA when a GPU is present. `TV->cp` and `TV->H` are computed in
`DeviceTest.thermo_x` but not asserted.

### Limits

`PXS->T` uses the frozen heat capacity as its slope, which is a hypothesis for slow convergence in saturated
parcels (not measured). It mutates its mole-fraction argument. The file written on non-convergence lands in the
working directory of the caller.
